picks.excerpt: MiniMax Music 3 lands as an open-weights text-to-music model that generates full five-minute songs locally, with ComfyUI and Diffusers workflows that run on a single 24GB GPU.
picks.rationale: First open-weights model that writes full five-minute songs on one 24GB GPU — moves generation off subscription platforms and onto the producer's own machine.

picks.excerpt: Ohlhorst Digital's Trama is a free offline stem separator for Windows, macOS and Linux that splits tracks into vocals, drums, bass and other using a fine-tuned Hybrid Transformer Demucs model — no uploads, no subscription.
picks.rationale: A free, fully offline Demucs-based splitter removes both the cost and the upload-your-masters risk from everyday remix, practice and sampling work.

picks.excerpt: ARIA sets new eligibility rules that exclude fully or mostly AI-generated recordings from Australia's official charts, while allowing AI-assisted human work.
picks.rationale: A national chart body now draws a hard line between AI-generated and AI-assisted, so how you declare AI use on a release decides whether it can chart at all.

picks.excerpt: Cyanite's Tagging 2.0 adds lyric analysis, tempo, vocal style, use-case and structural segmentation models plus a scalable API, reshaping how catalogues get searched and pitched.
picks.rationale: Lyric, vocal-style and section-level tagging behind an API changes how sync catalogues are searched and pitched — metadata work an artist or library can act on now.

picks.excerpt: A practical guide to getting artist and venue sites cited by AI assistants — structured data, canonical bios and the on-page work that decides what chatbots say about you.
picks.rationale: Concrete on-page steps — structured data, canonical bios — that decide what AI assistants say about an artist or venue when fans ask.
